en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Cittāgāra Vagga 47.
The Training Rule on Lodgings and Robes.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was using a lodging-cloth without relinquishing it.
Other bhikkhunīs who were menstruating could not obtain one.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as above]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā use a lodging-cloth without first relinquishing it? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā uses a lodging-cloth without first relinquishing it?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“…How, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā use a lodging-cloth without having relinquished it?
This, monks, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence…” [and so on].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule thus:
“Whichever nun, however, should use a lodging-cloth without having relinquished it, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whichever nun” means:
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... "a nun" ...pe...
this is the nun intended in this context.
“Residence robe” means:
it has been given [with the thought], “Let the nuns who are ill use it.
“Should use it without having relinquished it” means: [he uses it].
Having used it for two or three nights, if on the fourth day she washes it and uses it without having assigned it to a bhikkhunī, a sikkhamānā, or a sāmaṇerī, there is an offense of pācittiya.
If she uses it without having assigned it, perceiving that it has not been assigned, there is an offense of pācittiya.
If she uses it without having assigned it, being uncertain of it, there is an offense of pācittiya.
If she uses [an object] that has not been relinquished while perceiving it as having been relinquished, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she uses [an object] that has been relinquished while perceiving it as not having been relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she uses [an object] that has been relinquished while being doubtful [of its status], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it has been relinquished, there is no offense for one who perceives that it has been relinquished.
There is no offense if,
having relinquished it, one uses it.
Furthermore, she uses it by way of exchange;
there are no other bhikkhunīs who are menstruating;
[she uses it] when her robes have been stolen.
For one whose robes have been lost,
in times of distress,
for one who is insane,
"By one who is a first offender.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
